title: MDX
excerpt: How to set up a markdown-powered blog using Next.js, Tailwind CSS, and MDX

# How to Set Up a Markdown Blog Using Next.js, Tailwind CSS, and MDX This is how I built this website — a fully MDX‑powered blog running on the Next.js App Router.
--- # The Stack --- # Requirements & Installation You will need: - [Node.js](https://nodejs.org/en) - Optionally: [nvm](https://www.nvmnode.com/) Create a new Next.js project: ``` pnpm create next-app@latest my-app --yes ``` Install Tailwind CSS: ``` pnpm install tailwindcss @tailwindcss/postcss postcss ``` And import it in your global stylesheet: ```css:title=global.css @import "tailwindcss"; ``` --- # Project strucure This project uses the Next.js [App Router](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure), meaning routing is filesystem-based. Here's the simplified folder layout: ```bash └── project/ ├── app/ │ ├── blog/ │ │ ├── page.tsx <- Blog Homepage │ │ ├── [slug]/ │ │ │ └── page.tsx <- Single blog render │ ├── page.tsx │ └── layout.tsx ├── content/ │ └── │ └── page.mdx <- Article Content └── components/ ├── navbar.tsx └── Codeblock.tsx ``` ### /App The app/ folder is the core of routing: - `app/page.tsx` → renders the homepage (/) - `app/layout.tsx` → shared layout (navigation, footer, wrappers) ### /App/Blog The blog system is entirely filesystem-driven: - app/blog/page.tsx renders the blog homepage (/blog) showing all posts - `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx` dynamic route for individual blog posts - The [slug] folder matches the slug of each blog post in content/ - Example: `content/terraform-backend/page.mdx` →/blog/terraform-backend - Example: `content/ephemeral/page.mdx` /blog/ephemeral Content for each post lives in `content//page.mdx`, which is imported and rendered via Contentlayer This setup allows you to add a new blog post simply by creating a new folder in content/ — no changes to routing are required. MDX files act like pages — no extra configuration needed once MDX is set up. ### /components Contains shared UI components such as a navigation bar & MDX components such as code block and image ### Other files - `tailwind.config.ts` - Tailwind CSS configuration - `next.config.ts` - Next.js configuration including MDX setup - `package.json` - dependencies and scripts - `mdx.d.ts` - MDX TypeScript support - `mdx-components.tsx` - overrides and custom components for MDX (links, images, code blocks, etc.) - `contentlayer.config.ts` – configuration for Contentlayer, defining where your content lives (content/), the structure of your MDX documents, and any computed fields like slugs. It tells Contentlayer how to read, parse, and generate React-ready data from your MDX files. --- # MDX ## install mdx dependencies ``` pnpm add @next/mdx @mdx-js/loader @mdx-js/react @types/mdx ``` ## Configure next.config.tsx ```tsx:title=next.config.tsx import createMDX from '@next/mdx' import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig = { pageExtensions: ['js', 'jsx', 'ts', 'tsx', 'md', 'mdx'], output: 'export', // Added for Azure static storage support } satisfies NextConfig export default createMDX({ extension: /\.(md|mdx)$/, })(nextConfig) ``` ## Add & Configure mdx-components.tsx ```tsx:title=mdx-components.tsx import type { MDXComponents } from 'mdx/types' const components: MDXComponents = {} export function useMDXComponents(): MDXComponents { return components } ``` ## Configure contentlayer.config.ts Keep in mind this contains support for metadata in the mdx file ```tsx:title=contentlayer.config.ts import { defineDocumentType, makeSource } from "contentlayer/source-files"; export const Post = defineDocumentType(() => ({ name: "Post", filePathPattern: `**/page.mdx`, contentType: "mdx", fields: { title: { type: "string", required: true }, date: { type: "string", required: true }, excerpt: { type: "string", required: true }, }, computedFields: { slug: { type: "string", resolve: (doc) => doc._raw.flattenedPath.replace("/page", ""), }, url: { type: "string", resolve: (doc) => `/blog/${doc._raw.flattenedPath.replace("/page", "")}`, }, }, })); export default makeSource({ contentDirPath: "content", documentTypes: [Post], }); ``` ## Create a blog homepage & blog example Create a new folder under app called /blog and add a page.tsx. This solution links to the name of your blog folder. ### page.tsx ``` import Link from "next/link"; import { allPosts } from "../../.contentlayer/generated" export default function BlogPage() { const posts = allPosts.sort( (a, b) => new Date(b.date).getTime() - new Date(a.date).getTime() ); return (

Blog

Welcome to the blog section. Here you'll find all published articles.

    {posts.map((post) => (

  • {post.title}

    {post.description}

    • ))}
); } ``` # Troubleshooting ## This build is using turbopack To fix, implement the `--webpack` in the package.json on the run & build command # Sources used: - [Next.js Docs](https://nextjs.org/docs) - [Tailwindcss Docs](https://tailwindcss.com/docs/installation/framework-guides/nextjs) - [How to use markdown and MDX in Next.js](https://nextjs.org/docs/pages/guides/mdx) - [How I Built My Blog (original)](https://www.joshwcomeau.com/blog/how-i-built-my-blog/) - [How I Built My Blog](https://www.joshwcomeau.com/blog/how-i-built-my-blog-v2/) - [Guide to Writing MDX and Markdown](https://kabartolo.github.io/chicago-docs-demo/docs/mdx-guide/writing/)

  },\r
